title: Preventive maintenance schedule that updates as tasks close
summary: A static PM example distinguishes completion-based intervals from fixed-calendar and usage-based schedules.

blocks.title: The schedule is a consequence of the work
blocks.body: This is a static worked schedule, not a task system. Closing a task can set the next due date for completion-based maintenance; fixed-calendar and meter-based tasks need different rules. Select the rule from the equipment requirements and approved maintenance program.

blocks.heading: The board, Thursday morning
blocks.caption: Fictional date arithmetic for completion-based example tasks. No dates are recalculated here; intervals are not equipment recommendations.

blocks.heading: Choose the scheduling rule before automating it
items: Record actual completion, responsible person and evidence without erasing the original due date.
Completion-based: next due = actual close + interval, when the approved program permits it.
Fixed-calendar: retain the required calendar cadence. A late completion must not silently extend a mandatory deadline.
Usage-based: calculate from the relevant meter and record its reading; calendar arithmetic alone is insufficient.

blocks.title: The overdue line is the feature, not the failure
blocks.body: The backlash check is a day late and the board says so in plain text. A schedule that hides lateness teaches people to ignore it; a schedule that shows one red line among seven healthy ones teaches people to trust it. Trust is what makes the green lines mean anything.

nodes.title: Task comes due
nodes.detail: Computed, not remembered - it appears because the last close plus the interval says so.

nodes.title: Work gets done
nodes.detail: Or it visibly does not - both outcomes stay on the board.

nodes.title: Close with date and name
nodes.detail: The closing event is the only write to the schedule.

nodes.title: Next due computes itself
nodes.detail: Apply the task’s approved completion-based, fixed-calendar or meter-based rule; preserve overdue history.

items.label: Read the overdue and due-this-week lines only
items.detail: The rest of the board is doing its job; do not audit what is healthy.

items.label: Assign every due task to a name, not to 'the shop'
items.detail: A task with no name is a task with a date and a hope.

items.label: Ask why about anything overdue twice in a row
items.detail: Chronic lateness means the interval is wrong, the task is wrong, or the staffing is - the schedule just told you which assets to ask about.
